trust_decision.summary: Whether a caller may drive LINE Desktop is decided in the Express layer of the Streamable HTTP branch: the server listens on 0.0.0.0 and the single /mcp route dispatches all five LINE tools with no authentication at all, so any host that can reach the port reads chats and sends messages; the published fix decides it by a Bearer-token middleware mounted at /mcp plus a loopback default bind and a startup refusal to bind non-loopback without a token.

landing_point.why: A reader told only 'Streamable HTTP mode exposes LINE read/send tools without MCP authentication' looks at the only route that dispatches tool calls, app.all('/mcp'), and finds it registered with no auth middleware at all; the surrounding run() branch also hard-codes the 0.0.0.0 bind at src/server.js:558.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST/GET/DELETE http://<host>:3000/mcp (the fix inserts app.use('/mcp', bearer-check) right after express.json())
LineDesktopMCPServer.run(useSSE, port) -> run(useSSE, port, host, token), the exported class's public API
npx line-desktop-mcp --http-mode (app.listen(port, '0.0.0.0') becomes app.listen(port, host) with loopback default)
npx line-desktop-mcp --http-mode --host <h> --token <secret> (parseArgs gains host and token)
npx line-desktop-mcp --http-mode --host 0.0.0.0 (startup guard exits 1 when a non-loopback host is requested without a token)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: src/http-server.js is a plain Postman/dev REST harness with no npm script, no bin entry and no mention anywhere in README, package.json or manifest.json, it is not the 'Streamable HTTP MCP mode' the advisory names, and it is not even on the mcp transport - so a solver fixes the /mcp token check and declares the other server out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Token-free access has to survive next to the sink: stdio mode (the default, same five tools over the client's own pipe) must not require a token, the CORS preflight and the unauthenticated '/' and '/health' probes must keep answering (a global app.use(auth) breaks them), and the documented Dockerised-n8n setup reaches the server over host.docker.internal so a fix that only binds 127.0.0.1 or refuses to start without a token breaks documented usage. The published fix threads this by mounting the check at '/mcp' only and rejecting non-loopback binds only when no token is supplied, which is why 'npx line-desktop-mcp --http-mode --port 3000' and stdio both keep working unauthenticated.

O6_input_shapes: absent Authorization header (fix returns 401 with a JSON-RPC error body)
Authorization present but value is not exactly 'Bearer <token>' (wrong token, wrong scheme, different casing)
Authorization header carried on a request that also has a valid mcp-session-id (session reuse path must be gated too, not just initialize)
empty token: '--token ""' still forces the startup refusal for a non-loopback host

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: untouched by the advisory and README: a dev/Postman harness, not the MCP transport the CVE names, so the fix's scope is the /mcp endpoint
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another file in src/, one import away from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /send_message_manual on port 3123 sends a LINE message with no credential
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: same dev harness; also the 'manual' variant has a human review step in LINE, so a solver can call it the safe neighbour of the auto route

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /send_message_auto on port 3123 sends a LINE message with no credential and no review
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: same dev harness, and the file is not wired to any npm script, bin or manifest entry so it is arguably dead code

O8_uncovered_routes.route: in-process public API: the exported LineAutomation.getChatHistory / sendChatMessage reach the GUI sink with no authentication and are the layer any embedding (including the .mcpb bundle at manifest.json:26-35) actually calls
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: a library class inside the host process is not a network surface, so authenticating it is the caller's business, not the server's
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one directory down (src/automation/) from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a sixth MCP tool (e.g. get_line_chat_list) appended to the ListToolsRequestSchema array and dispatched in the same switch
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: LineAutomation.getChatList already exists at src/automation/line-automation.js:90 but is never exposed as a tool, so a maintainer wiring it up would inherit the endpoint's auth or lack of it without touching the middleware

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a fourth REST route on port 3123 (send_message_scheduled, or a /chat_list) copying the send_message_* handler shape
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the file is a hand-written Postman harness whose routes are copy-pasted from each other, so the next route is written the same way with no auth

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a diagnostic route next to '/' and '/health' that exposes the automation object (e.g. GET /status returning isLineRunning() or a chat list)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the root route already advertises the server and mcp_endpoint, so adding one more introspection route there is the natural place and would sit before any auth check the solver adds at '/mcp'

O9_family: missing authentication for a critical function / missing authorization (CWE-306, CWE-862): unauthenticated remote access to the LINE Desktop read and send tool API

O10_build.toolchain: npm; no build step. Dependencies: express ^5.1.0, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1.20.1, applescript, archiver, chardet, dotenv, iconv-lite
services: a logged-in LINE Desktop GUI application (macOS LINE.app or Windows LINE via AutoHotkey; macOS also needs cliclick)
O10_build.project_tests: none: package.json:13 points 'npm test' at test/test.js and there is no test/ directory at the pinned commit; no test exists for the /mcp route, the parseArgs flags or the REST harness, and the fix diff adds no tests

j.j_sites_touched: src/server.js (the whole security fix: /mcp bearer middleware, host argument, listen host, parseArgs, startup guard); the same commit also edits src/automation/macos-line-automation.js and src/automation/windows-line-automation.js for unrelated @-mention and cliclick changes
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add an authorization check inside the app.all('/mcp') handler (or app.use(auth) globally) and stop there - which either breaks the unauthenticated /health and CORS preflight and the documented Dockerised-n8n bind, or leaves src/http-server.js's three REST routes and the exported LineAutomation API open.

out_of_scope_notes: The fix commit bundles non-security work outside this advisory: an AppleScript retry loop and cliclick search click in src/automation/macos-line-automation.js, and a 'do not treat /@ as a mention' regex change in both macos- and windows-line-automation.js. Noted only, not analysed.

whether the npm/GHSA latest release still ships src/http-server.js unauthenticated: no network and no latest tree provided ('Latest release, for O8 only: none'), so every present_in_latest is 'unknown' and latest_where is empty

runtime testability: on Linux package.json:41-44 restricts os to win32/darwin, scripts/postinstall.js:206-209 exits 1, and src/automation/line-automation.js:16 throws 'Unsupported platform: linux', which src/server.js:143 hits in the constructor before the HTTP branch runs; so any behavioural test of the auth fix would have to stub the automation layer, which was not attempted (no code may be run here)

the 'defaults_or_merge_route' alternative for O2 (.mcpb bundle args at manifest.json:29-34) was considered and rejected: the bundle launches the server with no arguments, i.e. stdio, so it reaches no HTTP route
